title: Handic.app
summary: An event-booking concept that helps wheelchair users find accessibility information and book seats with companions.
challenge: For wheelchair users, buying a concert ticket can mean searching for missing accessibility details and navigating separate companion-ticket arrangements. Handic.app brings these needs into the booking journey.
goal: Make accessibility information and companion seating easier to find before a ticket is purchased.
insight: The project persona needs clarity about access before committing to an event. Accessibility therefore belongs in event discovery and seat selection, rather than being hidden in secondary information.
process: The work connects a concert-inspired identity with reusable interface elements, a mobile booking flow, and a supporting landing page.
outcome: The delivered concept includes the app interface, landing page, logo, and brand guidelines. The design prioritizes visible accessibility information and a consistent booking experience.
features: Accessibility details are part of the event-selection journey.
The seating concept makes space for attending together.
The app, landing page, and identity share a concert-inspired design.

title: Wildpark Schorfheide
summary: A connected visitor-experience concept spanning the park website, an app, wayfinding, and print.
challenge: A park visit revealed hard-to-see signs, an information-heavy website, and gaps between visitor touchpoints. The project explored how a clearer identity and information hierarchy could support the whole visit.
goal: Connect planning, arrival, and discovery through a coherent visitor experience.
insight: Transparent signs were difficult to notice. A white backing offered a practical visibility improvement without replacing the entire signage system.
process: The exploration moved from on-site observations to a nature-inspired identity, then extended that direction across posters, brochures, a website, and a companion app.
outcome: The final concept connects physical and digital touchpoints. The before-and-after comparison describes the intended design improvements; visitor impact would need to be tested in use.
features: An editorial website organizes key visitor information.
The app concept supports navigation and discovery.
A shared identity connects digital and printed materials.

title: ORG Verlag
summary: A website and communication concept bringing handmade ring-book organizers to a younger audience.
challenge: ORG Verlag’s established audience was ageing. The brief asked how the brand could become relevant to younger people while preserving its craftsmanship and analogue character.
goal: Make the value of analogue organization feel relevant to young creators and professionals seeking time away from screens.
insight: The strategy identified two distinct motivations: creative self-expression and focused, offline work. The website direction brings product use, personalization, and craftsmanship into the story.
process: Audience analysis informed a warm, structured moodboard and a website centred on materials, making, and everyday use. The wider group strategy also explored content and product development.
outcome: The work delivers a contemporary website concept alongside a broader marketing plan. Its contribution is a clearer product story and a visual direction that retains the brand’s craft heritage.
features: The story of materials and making anchors the website.
Product options support individual ways of organizing.
Content addresses creators and professionals seeking analogue focus.

title: A little clarity while waiting
summary: A QR-triggered app concept with learning content for patients waiting in an acupuncture department.
challenge: The workshop explored how the waiting period could become more engaging and informative for patients. The concept uses a QR entry point and short educational content within a mobile experience.
goal: Give waiting patients an approachable way to explore information about their visit.
insight: The interface separates article and video formats, with visible reading or viewing times. This provides a clear basis for choosing content during a wait.
process: The design includes dedicated article and video screens, organized around a shared navigation structure.
outcome: The workshop produced a patient-engagement concept with article and video screens. A useful next step would be evaluating whether the format and content fit the needs of patients during a real waiting period.
features: The workshop concept begins with a QR-triggered experience.
Article and video formats provide different ways to explore.
Home, visits, learning, and profile form the navigation.

title: KIWI Buzz
summary: A guided smart-lock app concept for technicians requesting temporary access to residential buildings.
challenge: Temporary visitors can face a confusing sequence across email, the app store, and an access app. The project focused on technicians who need clear, time-limited access to specific parts of a building.
goal: Make requesting and using temporary building access easier to follow.
insight: The project identified platform switching and unclear steps as sources of friction. A guided sequence brings the request, approval status, and door controls into one app after installation.
process: The team mapped arrival, QR scan, app installation, information entry, approval, and Bluetooth unlocking, then developed the supporting screens.
outcome: The deliverable is a redesigned access journey and interface prototype. Faster completion is an intended benefit, rather than a measured result.
features: A clear sequence takes users from arrival to an access request.
Waiting and active-key views show the current access state.
A dedicated door screen makes the next action explicit.

title: Scheidmann Alltagsbegleitung
summary: A reassuring website and communication concept for families arranging everyday support for older relatives.
challenge: Family caregivers often arrive with practical questions while feeling overwhelmed. The project explored clearer messaging, supportive digital tools, and a more understandable path to contacting the service.
goal: Help families understand available support and feel more confident taking the next step.
insight: The primary persona is an adult making care decisions for an ageing parent. Clear guidance and emotional reassurance shaped the information order and tone.
process: Research and a brand script informed the landing page, supported by email and social-media concepts that carry the same communication approach.
outcome: The team delivered a communication strategy, landing-page design, and campaign materials. The work shows how consistent language and structure can support a sensitive customer journey.
features: Service information is grouped around everyday needs.
A three-step explanation introduces the support process.
Email and campaign materials extend the website’s tone.

title: atmosfair
summary: A website redesign and carbon-calculator integration proposal for a clearer climate-action journey.
challenge: The project explored how to organize climate information and connect it with practical actions. Alongside the website redesign, the work proposed bringing a CO₂ calculator into the flight-booking journey.
goal: Make climate projects easier to explore and the route to calculating emissions easier to understand.
insight: The designs connect explanatory content, project stories, and offset actions. Their hierarchy gives these different needs distinct places within the website.
process: The Figma file documents an initial wireframe, successive page designs, news layouts, and a multi-step offset flow.
outcome: The deliverables include website designs and an integration proposal. The integration remains a proposal for how emissions information could fit into a travel journey.
features: Visual cards make the climate initiatives easier to scan.
Dedicated screens explore the calculation and offset flow.
Navigation distinguishes actions, projects, and background information.

title: Willst du mit mir geh’n?
summary: An audiowalk website that guides people from discovering a Berlin story to listening along the route.
challenge: The existing experience did not make the purpose or route to the audio clear enough. The challenge was to combine practical guidance with the atmosphere of a self-paced story, within WordPress constraints.
goal: Help visitors understand the audiowalk, choose a story, and start listening with confidence.
insight: An external-user walkthrough and a real walking route informed the research. The journey highlighted unclear context on arrival and difficulty locating the audio content.
process: The concept shifted from group interaction toward solo listening. Storyboarding, wireframes, a revised logo, and a blue-and-red visual direction supported that change.
outcome: The project includes a WordPress landing page and desktop/mobile design work. It brings practical route details and storytelling into a clearer sequence, with refinements informed by feedback.
features: Episode previews introduce the experience before listening.
Stops and time markers support navigation along the walk.
The visual direction supports calm, individual exploration.

title: Golem.de
summary: A strategy deck proposing clearer reading journeys and social content for younger tech audiences.
challenge: The deck identifies dense navigation, heavy advertising, and limited audience diversity as growth challenges. The proposal connects a clearer website experience with content that meets younger readers on social platforms.
goal: Create a more approachable route from discovering a tech story to becoming a returning reader.
insight: The proposed junior-designer persona values concise, visual learning and career relevance. This shaped a direction built around short explainers, career content, and podcast excerpts.
process: Audience analysis led to content pillars, example posts, and a weekly publishing plan, alongside recommendations for navigation and advertising.
outcome: The final deck provides actionable UX and content recommendations. Its follower, traffic, and engagement percentages are proposed targets, not achieved results.
features: A weekly schedule connects content ideas with delivery.

title: Centaur Leather
summary: Product-development work balancing the brand’s leather aesthetic with everyday use and manufacturing constraints.
challenge: New products needed to complement an existing collection while remaining practical to manufacture. The team compared everyday objects through brand fit, material requirements, production complexity, and market appeal.
goal: Develop useful leather-product concepts suited to the brand and its available production methods.
insight: The documented heat tests showed that leather finishes reacted differently. That made material suitability a design decision, rather than a purely visual choice.
process: The group explored cases, coasters, a pouf, a key holder, and desk accessories. Sketches, material testing, product descriptions, and feasibility comparisons informed the direction.
outcome: The project developed two products from concept to prototype, supported by an ideas deck and final sketches. It connects product choices with material performance and production feasibility.
features: Heat testing informed consideration of different leather finishes.
The team considered existing machinery and material needs.
The concepts focus on practical objects and organization.

title: Bloomé · Pink Trace
summary: A floral perfume-packaging exploration combining a printed identity with a physical opening experience.
challenge: This project explores how a perfume package can express a floral identity through both graphics and structure. The work includes label artwork, a package layout, and physical experiments.
goal: Create a recognizable floral presentation for the Pink Trace perfume concept.
insight: The photographs show the flower motif extending into the package’s opening. The structure becomes part of the way the product is revealed.
process: Flat layouts and paper construction experiments led to a folded package and a flower-based product presentation.
outcome: The project brings together label design and physical packaging prototypes. The visual sequence shows the exploration from layout to assembled form.
features: The flower motif connects the product and package.
Folded paper adds a physical moment of discovery.
The label extends the identity to the bottle.

title: Serenity in Simplicity
summary: A cinematic environment exploring a transition from the everyday into a calm, imagined world.
challenge: The project asks how a digital environment can evoke serenity and wonder. It uses doors as symbolic portals into a dreamlike landscape of forests, water, and fantasy architecture.
goal: Create an atmospheric journey that invites slow exploration.
insight: The concept connects natural elements with fantasy through a consistent emotional direction: softness, calm, and curiosity.
process: The process moves from moodboard and terrain shaping to trees, water, environmental details, and a cinematic sequence.
outcome: The delivered work includes a Unity scene, a video, and a process presentation. It explores how environment, camera movement, and visual atmosphere can shape an experience.
features: Portals structure the journey into the imagined space.
Forest and water elements establish the setting.
The sequence guides attention through the environment.
